method: Read all 730 source entries. Semantically checked every initial answer and all four options (727 synonym rows and 661 antonym rows). Rechecked every changed or added final row and all four final options after regeneration. Unchanged rows verified byte-for-byte at parsed row level against the initial reviewed snapshot. Structural checks run separately.

editorialAntonymExclusions.reason: A composed work is not the opposite of decomposition, which names a different process.
A moral faculty is not the opposite of immoral behaviour.
A business or project has no simple lexical opposite; inactivity contrasts with initiative, a different sense.
Confusion can persist despite an explanation and is not its antonym.
Customer is a reciprocal role, not an opposite; a merchant is also a buyer.
Clothing and the state of nakedness are not matching lexical opposites.
Secular writing is a contrasting category, not a lexical opposite of sacred writings.
A beckoning gesture has no clear antonym among the supplied nouns.
A mismatch is not an antonym of a completing or enhancing addition.
Extinguishment ends a fire; it is not the antonym of a fire.
Neglect is not an antonym of assessment.
The open sea is a contrasting location, not an antonym of a port.
Closure is an action or state, not the lexical opposite of a surgical cut.
Visitors are contrasting occupants; the roles are not lexical opposites.
Bleach removes colour but is not an antonym of a colouring substance.
A closure is not the lexical opposite of a narrow cut.
A seal closes a vent; this is an association rather than an antonym.
Seal is an action or object, not an antonym of a crack.
A solid surface is not a lexical antonym of a crack.
Adult and infant flank adolescence; neither is a unique lexical opposite.
A part and its whole are a relation, not antonyms.
A mansion differs in size and quality but is not a lexical antonym of a hut.
Attic is a contrasting location, not a lexical antonym of basement.
An idea or belief can be factual; fact is not its antonym.
Stag is a male counterpart, not a lexical antonym of female deer.
Principal is a represented role, not a lexical antonym of representative.
Clean mark is not an established opposite of stain.
Pleasure is a feeling, not the lexical opposite of a routine task.
Both hot and cold contrast with lukewarm; no unique directional opposite exists.
Foreign contrasts with the national sense, which is absent from the taught household definition.

residualLimitations: Words are sense-dependent; judgments concern the ordinary teaching sense or specified context, not interchangeability in every sentence.
Some distractors differ in part of speech; difficulty has not been psychometrically calibrated.
Original source explanations remain unchanged, including relations excluded from the question bank.
Any later CSV changes require renewed semantic review.

postReviewChanges.difficultyNote: Levels are not assigned by hand. Regenerating data/word-levels/levels.json re-banded all 864 words, so the five original bands were renumbered from 146 words each to 150/149/150/149/149. The 17 new words landed in Levels 1 to 5 by the documented frequency-and-length score, not all in the last level: hostile in Level 1, abundant and porous in Level 2, ascend, propel and heinous in Level 3, resolute, tenacious, intrepid, meander, scurry, opulent and adversity in Level 4, and taciturn, apprehensive, trudge and abhorrent in Level 5.

postReviewChanges.reason: Synonym and antonym prompts no longer restate the word's own definition. Many prompts ended in a parenthetical sense tag that was a verbatim or near-verbatim copy of the taught meaning, for example "Choose the synonym for 'especially' (More than usual, or more than other things.)." Showing the meaning turned a recall-the-synonym task into a match-the-definition task.
postReviewChanges.rule: A sense tag was kept only where it selects one genuine sense of a polysemous word and does not restate the meaning or contain the answer. It was removed where it covered 60 percent or more of the meaning's content words, or where it contained the correct answer as a phrase.

postReviewChanges.verification: Only the problem text changed. Every option list, correct answer, row type, target word, row order and row count is byte-identical to the previous version, and all 1511 rows still have four distinct options with exactly one correct answer. Definition questions are unchanged and still show the definition, because matching a definition to its word is the task being tested there.
postReviewChanges.reviewStatus: This was an editorial prompt change, not new content, so it was applied mechanically and verified structurally. The retained sense tags were not re-reviewed for sense accuracy.
